set_aside.subject: repeatability-guarantee applicability
set_aside.text: Every promise in these documents that a function repeats itself — equal outputs on equal inputs, a repaired slot staying repaired, a verdict that holds — is a promise about code that obtains neither.
set_aside.question: How is it determined and recorded whether an implementation obtains time or chance, and therefore whether its repeatability promises apply, when the preceding sentence says alternative ways of obtaining them are not detected?
options: Coverage is an unverified author-side assumption and is never represented by the kernel.
Coverage is inferred only from observed outputs, with a named status when conflicting observations occur.
Implementations capable of obtaining time or chance must be refused by some additional check.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat coverage as an unverified assumption; record ordinary trial and execution results without claiming that the implementation is repeatable.

witness.initial: A contract has a trial case, and an implementation obtains chance through a route the sandbox does not detect.
events: The kernel runs the corpus once; the chance-dependent output happens to satisfy every case.
The kernel admits and activates the implementation.
The owner or agent inspects the implementation's verdict and activation.
outcomes: The kernel reports an ordinary admitted verdict and activation, with no indication that the repeatability promises do not apply.
The kernel reports or stores that repeatability coverage is unknown or absent, because that fact controls whether the verdict holds.
witness.observer: The owner or agent deciding whether the activation or verdict can be relied upon

set_aside.subject: meaning of obtaining time or chance
set_aside.question: Is this condition about the implementation being incapable of obtaining time or chance, about a particular execution not actually obtaining them, or about no observed execution having obtained them?
options: The promise applies only to implementations that can never obtain either value.
The promise is decided separately for each execution path.
The promise applies until an execution is observed obtaining or reflecting either value.
set_aside.default_guess: Interpret it as a property of the implementation across all executions, because equal-output and lasting-verdict promises span executions.

witness.initial: An implementation reads an alternative clock only when its Boolean input is true; the corpus and first real runs use false.
events: The agent submits the implementation and the kernel admits it on false inputs.
A flow runs the function twice with the same false input.
Later a flow runs it twice with the same true input.
outcomes: Because the code can obtain time, none of the implementation's executions are covered by the repeatability promises.
The false-input executions are covered because those executions obtain no time, while the true-input executions are not.
witness.observer: The owner or agent interpreting the verdict and traces

set_aside.subject: observed breach of repeatability
set_aside.text: a repaired slot staying repaired, a verdict that holds
set_aside.question: What action, observable state change, or failure follows if an admitted and active implementation later gives unequal outputs for equal inputs or fails a case over which its stored verdict was admitted?
options: Nothing automatic happens; the execution is judged independently and the stored verdict and activation remain usable.
The execution fails and invalidates the verdict or activation.
The execution fails but changes the corpus or verdict only if an authorized actor captures it.
set_aside.default_guess: Fail only the current execution; leave the stored verdict and activation unchanged unless the failure is explicitly captured, because no invalidation action is named.

witness.initial: A chance-dependent implementation has an admitted verdict, is active, and previously succeeded for input X.
events: An owner or agent runs a flow that invokes it again with X.
The implementation produces a different result or violates the expected case because its hidden chance source changed.
An agent later requests rollback to that implementation, whose recorded verdict is still admitted over the current corpus.
outcomes: The differing execution is only a failed execution; the stored admitted verdict still permits rollback because rollback runs no admission.
The observation means the verdict no longer holds, so rollback is refused or the activation is invalidated.
witness.observer: The actor running the flow or requesting rollback
